faqs.q: Who is eligible to participate in HACK_NEXUS 1.0?
faqs.a: Any enrolled undergraduate or postgraduate student from a recognised college or university in India can take part. Squads have 2 or 3 members, and squads from different departments or years are welcome.

faqs.q: When do we get the problem statements and tracks?
faqs.a: Problem statements and tracks will be given on the spot, when the sprint begins at 9:30 AM on October 8. They are not shared before the event, so come with your squad, your laptops and an open mind.

faqs.q: Can we use pre-existing codebases or templates?
faqs.a: Write all of your core problem logic during the 10-hour sprint. Open-source libraries, UI components and framework starters (such as Next.js, FastAPI or Vite) are allowed.

faqs.q: What is provided at the venue?
faqs.a: Each squad gets a desk in the CAR Lab or Garuda Lab with an internet connection and power. Lunch and refreshments are provided.

faqs.q: How does the finalist round work?
faqs.a: At the 7:30 PM code freeze, shortlisted squads are announced. They present in the finalist round on October 9 (9:30 AM – 2:00 PM, Watson Lab): a 5-minute live demo of the prototype, then a 2-minute Q&A with the industry panel. Squads are judged on innovation, technical implementation, functionality, problem-solving approach and presentation.

faqs.q: Does the 10-hour clock pause for lunch?
faqs.a: No. The sprint runs without a break from 9:30 AM to 7:30 PM. Lunch and refreshments are provided, so take breaks in turns.
